summary: This sermon introduces the Psalms of Ascent (120-134), ancient traveling songs sung by pilgrims journeying to Jerusalem, and applies them to the Christian life as a communal pilgrimage. The preacher contrasts being a tourist (focused on sights and comfort) with being a pilgrim (focused on transformation and discovery), arguing that discipleship happens along the road, not just at the destination.
key_points: Psalms 120-134 were worship songs for pilgrims traveling to Jerusalem for feasts
The Christian life is a pilgrimage, not a destination—God shapes us on the journey
Psalm 120 begins with crying out in distress, the first step of discipleship
Discipleship is communal; we need traveling companions and cannot journey alone
Psalm 121 lifts eyes to God who keeps and watches over us on the road
Spiritual growth requires slow, costly perseverance, not microwavable Christ-likeness
big_idea: The Christian life is a pilgrimage where God shapes us along the journey through community, hardship, and perseverance, not just at the final destination, and we must trust Him and walk together every step of the way.
title: Summer in Psalms: PSALMS 120-121
